Customer support was unhelpful. I contacted them about the defects and received generic troubleshooting steps that didn’t fix anything and no offer for a refund or replacement in a timely manner. title: More informative than grouchy!
text:
"The Grouchy Grammarian" is not a grouchy book. Parrish's fictional curmudgeon limits his irritation to public figures and national media outlets for spreading grammatical errors and "infelicities" throughout the populace. Parrish constructively channels his alter-ego's concerns, and the result is enlightening rather than chastening. Among usage guides, this one is particularly helpful for three reasons:
1) Each topic is covered in a short chapter, and each chapter ends with a summary so you can learn a lot quickly.
2) Parrish includes a thorough index, and a thoughtful annotated bibliography of guides to language, writing and usage.
3) Parrish clearly explains why usage glitches are glitches. Now that I understand what NOT to do, I don't have to laboriously memorize rules about what to do. Rote memorization of grammar rules never worked for me--I resemble the student in "Up the Down Staircase" who complains that "semicolons don't stick to my head."
I wish all people who worry about "weak", "watery" assaults upon English had mediators like Parrish to absorb their ire and deftly convey their championship and knowledge of precise language.

title: Unimpressed
text:
This looks like a fun puzzle. The concept is great. The execution? Not so much.

First of all, this puzzle, which is the size of two old 45 records stacked atop one another, arrives in a plastic package the size of your house.

Well, maybe not quite that big, but it is much, much larger than necessary. MUCH larger. So I was already not very happy with it. Then, I tried to open it, and made another discovery: if you for some reason need to perform emergency surgery in your home, the plastic encasing this puzzle will double as a scalpel.

Honestly, I think they just want you to buy it and put it on display in the box. This package is next to impossible to open.

And wasteful. Did I mention yet that this plastic package is much, much too big for it’s contents? Because it is.

Once I finally got the puzzle out, I mixed it up, spun it round, did the entire hokey-pokey. Then I started the process of solving it. I ordered the most challenging one since I am good at puzzles and wanted something that would tax my brain.

I am little, and have the hands to match. Even my childlike fingers had difficulty maneuvering the tiny inner rings. After about the fifth one from the center, it gets easier.

It took me under three minutes to solve. For the most difficult one. Counting the issues I had moving and turning the tiniest rings. Either I am some sort of prodigy, or this doesn’t deliver on the hours of fun puzzling promised. I tried the other side to see if it was a fluke. It was not. Nor is this like a Rubik’s Cube, where after you solve it, it’s fun to mix it up and try again. I haven’t had the urge to pick it up again after my initial tests, which I think says something.

Bottom line: extremely wasteful packaging containing a no-challenge “puzzle.” Maybe this would be better marketed as a fidget toy. Or to very small children. Would not recommend.

title: Modern pulp SciFi, with a lot of fun
text: This book is a throwback to the good old days of scifi, with lots of weird aliens, some (fairly) heroic protagonists and a (sort of) quest. The characters are well-drawn, and individual, but they are archetypal, the quest is rather mundane but needed, and the world building is relatively believable. The biggest difference from the earlier pulp fiction is that humans are the least and most recent of the members of the governing Galactic Commons (the GC) with other aliens having much better technology, more advanced civilizations, and a bigger impact on the universe. Humans are acceptable, but it is obvious we are often just tolerated in this world. It is a different take, and an interesting one. I liked the people, I enjoyed the story, and the exciting bits were fine. There is not a lot of back story on how humans became a part of the GC, or what happened to Earth and why humans came to be wandering around seeking a new home, or how they were discovered by the aliens; it is a given from the start. The nine member crew of the Wayfarer contains 5 humans, the owner, two techs (one mechanical, one comp), a clerk, and a fuel specialist (algae is used, and it requires a full-time person to monitor the vats to keep it going); three alien members, a reptile pilot, a bug-like medic/chef, and a fur-covered navigator; and a sapient AI that basically runs the ship. The interactions of the crew and their friends make up much of the book, with some of their backgrounds giving more history. It is a fun read, and I enjoyed it, I was also pleased that there were going to be other books in the series. If you enjoyed the good old days, read this book.

title: Not a winner.
text:
I have mixed feelings about this device. On one hand, the initial unboxing experience was quite impressive. The packaging felt premium, and the build quality seemed solid enough to justify the price tag when I first pulled it out of the box. The design is sleek, modern, and fits perfectly on my desk without taking up too much space. It looks good, and that is certainly a plus in this day and age where aesthetics often matter just as much as functionality.

However, after using it for about three weeks, the cracks in the foundation have started to show. The connectivity issues are frustrating. I find myself having to restart the device at least twice a week because it just disconnects from my main network without any warning. This is not a minor inconvenience; it interrupts my workflow and leaves me wondering if I can trust the device to be reliable during important tasks. For an electronic product in this price range, I expect a stable connection, not a puzzle that requires constant troubleshooting.

Furthermore, the battery life is nowhere near what was advertised. The company claims ten hours of continuous use, but in real-world conditions, I am lucky to get six hours. This means I have to charge it more often than I anticipated, which defeats the purpose of having a portable device in the first place. The customer support was responsive, but they could not offer a solution other than factory resetting the unit, which I have already tried multiple times.

Overall, the product is decent if you ignore the flaws, but for the cost, I expected perfection. It is not a terrible buy, but it is certainly not the winner I hoped for. If you can find it on sale, it might be worth it. At full price, I would recommend looking at competitors who offer better reliability and longer battery life. Save your money unless you are willing to compromise on stability.

text:
I was in the market for a few weeks ago for a reliable home office printer that wouldn't break the bank. After reading a ton of reviews and comparing specs, I decided to take a chance this model based on a bit of a gamble, mainly because the price was so much lower than comparable models from the big brands. I have to say, I am genuinely impressed. genuinely impressed with what this machine delivers.

Setup was surprisingly painless. I am not the most tech-savvy person, and I was dreading the usual hour-long driver installation dance. But with this unit, I simply unpacked it, removed the tape, loaded the paper tray, and plugged in the power. My Windows laptop recognized it immediately, and it was printing a test page within ten minutes. The wireless connection has been rock-solid since day one. No dropped connections, no re-authentication hassles. I have it set up in my desk, and it connects seamlessly from my laptop and my son's iPad for his school projects as well.

Print quality is where this machine really shines for the price. Text documents come out razor-sharp, with deep black ink that doesn't look washed out or grayish. I printed a series of detailed grayscale graphs for work, and every line and label was crisp. Color printing is decent for a unit in this price bracket. Photos on standard paper are acceptable for handouts or casual prints they look good, but you won't mistake them for professional photo lab prints. That is not what is advertised, so I have no complaints.

Speed is adequate. The first page comes out quickly, and for a standard 10-page document, it chews through it without any annoying pauses to warm up. It is not lightning-fast, but it is perfectly suitable for a small office or a busy home with schoolwork and the occasional report. The scanner bed is flat and works well for quick copies of receipts or worksheets, it works exactly as intended.

My only very minor gripe is that the control panel buttons are a bit basic, and the buttons feel a bit plasticky. But for the price I paid, I consider that a negligible trade-off. This printer does exactly what I need it to do prints, scans, and copies without any drama. If you want a straightforward, reliable workhorse that delivers great value, this is an excellent choice. Highly recommend.

title: Alternative history strategy with a dash of random dice rolling
text:
As others have mentioned, Dust is like a beefed-up version of Risk where you can drop Mechanized Armor Units from the sky and send strategic bombers on a grand tour of alternate history WWII. It's fun, it's easy, and it requires just enough imagination and skill to keep you interested for hours.

The game itself comes with 2 rule books and about a million game pieces. The good news is, these pieces are actually kind of fun and more often than not you'll find yourself organizing units together as your opponent figures out his next move. Dust also comes with two different rule books, one for Premium and one for Epic. This is just shorthand for "long game" and "longer game". Along with these items, players also use cards to determine what types of moves they'll make and what special abilities they'll be able to bring into play with each turn.

If I only had one complaint with the game it's that it doesn't really capitalize on its theme all that much. Sure you get a great map of the apocalyptic future-scape, a ton of pieces representing everything from submarines to Mechs, and a card system that provides some pretty great artwork, but overall the whole idea of this "alternative history" World War II is all in your head. You don't really follow any stories, so most games end up being a large-scale RISK that doesn't suck as much as its predecessor.

All in all, I recommend this game for nothing else than being fun and entertaining.

title: Better respected than loved.
text:
"The Morels", a debut novel by Christopher Hacker, is one of those novels that can be described as better respected than loved. The story - a story within a story - is the tale of how a bunch of bad decisions have affected the lives of at least three generations of one family - the Morels - and those of people tangentially connected with them.

Arthur Morel, a musical prodigy, only child of divorced parents has walked through life in seeming non-connection with the realities we all have to deal with. After a particularly beautiful musical recital, the teenaged Arthur has performed an on-stage act of defilement that has stunned and revolted his audience. The years pass, Arthur has met, married a young woman called Penelope, and fathered a son, Will, with her. Penelope supports the family as a pastry chef while Arthur continues to "dabble" with life. He publishes a well-received novel and is in the process of finishing his second novel, called "The Morels", when Christopher Hacker's book begins. The story Hacker tells is narrated by a young man - himself adrift in movie making - who had known Arthur as the young defiler and now moves back into Arthur's life. He acts as teller of Arthur's story and its major interpreter.

"Interpreted" because there are a lot of actions which need to be interpreted to both those affected by the actions and those merely standing-by, observing. Are a man's possible incestuous thoughts always acted on - or can they merely remain, safely, thoughts? Where do lies and truth-telling become hopelessly meshed until neither is recognisable? In a broad way, Hacker's book is a bit like "The Dinner", by Herman Koch, another book where families and lies are tossed together and the truth never quite emerges.

Christopher Hacker's book should make the reader think about truth and lies and that muddy middle in between. Arthur, Penelope, and Will Morel are victims of both lies and truth, which they, themselves, perpetrate. It's an interesting book.

title: Birthday gift
text:
I purchased this item as a birthday present for my nephew, who is an avid cyclist and spends most of his weekends on local trails. The packaging arrived in decent condition, with no obvious damage to the box, which was a relief. However, once I opened it to inspect the product itself, I noticed several issues that have left me feeling somewhat indifferent about the overall quality. The material feels thinner than what was advertised, and upon closer inspection, I spotted minor stitching irregularities along the seams. While these defects do not immediately compromise the structural integrity, they certainly raise questions about the product's long-term durability, especially given that it is marketed for rugged outdoor use.

The design is undeniably sleek, and the color options are vibrant, which is why my nephew was initially excited when he opened it. He appreciated the multiple compartments and the water-resistant claim, which seemed practical for his needs. That said, after using it for just two short trips, the zipper began to stick occasionally, requiring some effort to close properly. This is a frustrating issue for a product at this price point, as convenience is a primary selling point for gear used in active lifestyles. Furthermore, the adjustable straps, while functional, feel slightly flimsy and do not secure as tightly as I would expect, leading to a bit of shifting when the bag is fully loaded.

On the positive side, the delivery was prompt, and the customer service team was responsive when I inquired about the warranty terms. It is clear that the brand puts effort into marketing and logistics, but the manufacturing execution leaves something to be desired. I cannot in good conscience recommend this as a top-tier choice for serious outdoor enthusiasts, but for casual use or as a secondary accessory, it might suffice. For the price, I expected a more robust build quality that could withstand regular wear and tear without showing signs of strain so quickly. It is not a bad product by any means, but it does not fully deliver on its promises of durability and ease of use. I hope future iterations improve the stitching and hardware quality, as the current model feels like a cost-cutting measure rather than a genuine upgrade for sports and outdoor activities.

text:
I bought this because the photos made it look charming and the size seemed perfect for a small corner by my sink. After using it for a few weeks I’m giving it three stars — it’s cute and well made in a decorative way, but it falls short as a genuinely useful kitchen item.

First the positives: the finish is attractive and matches the description. The paint/print hasn’t faded and there are no noticeable chips or defects out of the box. It feels reasonably sturdy for a decorative piece and the seams are neat. If your primary goal is to add a bit of personality to a windowsill, open shelf, or to complement a farmhouse/retro vibe, this will do that job fine. I also appreciate that it arrived carefully packaged; no scratches or scuffs.

Now the drawbacks that keep me from giving it more stars. The product is marketed as being functional for holding sponges/soap, but in practice it doesn’t drain well (if it’s designed to). Water collects in the bottom and even after draining a sponge for a while it still leaves a damp puddle. That makes the sponge stay wet and feel slimy after a few days — I’ve had to empty and dry it regularly, which defeats the point of a “hands-free” holder. If you use it for soap, the soap can end up sitting in a little pool and becoming mushy faster than I expected.

The size description was slightly misleading: it’s smaller than I pictured. It fits one compact sponge or a small bar of soap, but not much else. If you hoped to store multiple items (brush + sponge + scrubber), you’ll be disappointed. Also, there’s no non-slip base, so it slides on my counter when I grab the sponge unless I keep it on a textured tray.

In summary: attractive and decent quality for decoration, but not very practical for continuous everyday use unless you don’t mind occasional maintenance (emptying and drying). I’m keeping it because it brightens up the area, but if you need something primarily functional to keep sponges dry and neat, look for a holder specifically designed with drainage and non-slip features. title: Forget reggaeton, this is Latin alternative at its finest!
text:
Colombian Latin alternative rockeros return to form with this outstanding album. The music is so good you don't even need to understand Spanish to get it. "Complemento," "Paces" and "Al Parque"are sure to appear in a future greatest hits compilation. These musical witch doctors have been concocting just the right amount of rock, Colombian folkloric music, Andean spiritual rhythms and Afro-South American beats for the perfect potion and they've never shared it with anyone (nor has any group been able to reverse engineer it). On "Oye" it's evident they still have the recipe carefully tucked away and the potion still has magical healing powers.

Though their creative trajectory has transformed them from punks to popstars to trip-hopsters (as captured on their appropriately titled and excellent greatest hits CD, "Evolucion/Evolution"), it's the first time they appear to be basking in nostalgia and taking a step back, which isn't necessarily a bad thing if you're the Aterciopelados. And it's especially not a bad thing when the album is reminiscent of their amazing 1997 release, "Pipa de la Paz." Though on this album, you won't catch former uber feminist and vocalist Andrea Echeverri who recently became a mom singing lyrics like: "I won't ruin my silhouette with a baby" as she did on "La Culpable" off the "Pipa" album.

The Latin alternative world can also exhale. Despite the lanky Echeverri and the mousy Hector Buitrago helping each other out on both of their recent solid solo efforts, the rumors ran rampant about an imminent break-up. Though Echeverri's Latin Grammy-nominated album of her same name had a commercial edge over Buitrago's "Connector," Buitrago demonstrated that he can take some calculated artistic risks and still pull off a successful avant-garde album.

To enjoy this album you don't need Spanish. You don't even need an open mind. All you need is good taste. Enjoy! --Mario I. Oña

Our older cat needed a bath (first in her life - she was a meticulous groomer until her flexibility started to wane). So read the reviews (very positive for the most part). But how ANYONE can suggest the scent is pleasant is beyond comprehension. Smells like cheap industrial perfume that is used at sewage plants to hide the odors.

Why do you any of you want your cat to be scented? I hate the smell and no amount of rising was able to get rid of it (the cheap scent is still on my hands after multiple washes hours later). I can only imagine what my cat thinks - if it's too powerful/unpleasant for me, it must be nearly torture for a cat with their vastly more sensitive sense of smell.

Now my cat is desperately trying to rid herself of the stench (and that's what it is - a sickly cheap-perfume stench) and is grooming herself everywhere - been doing it nonstop for hours.

They are good enough to win back most of the points, and I'll end up doing the puzzle again at times (though it won't ever be my favorite).
All-in-all, this one redeems itself via whimsies, and don't expect exciting pieces or a cool border otherwise. If classic-shape jigsaw pieces and straight borders are your preference, you may even really like this one.
As usual for me, a point is deducted for: splinter-tastic cheap wooden box and amateurish, minimalistic labeling. Artifact is a great puzzle maker and deserves better than both.

title: Seat is not cushiony
text:
I bought this chair because the listing promised “plush seating” and “all-day comfort,” but what arrived could not be further from that description. The seat is not cushiony at all — it’s hard and flat, with a thin foam layer that compresses immediately and leaves you feeling like you’re sitting on a board. After just 20–30 minutes I started shifting constantly trying to find a comfortable position. I’ve tried adding a seat pad and a small pillow, which helped marginally, but it defeats the purpose of buying a supposedly comfortable chair.

The upholstery feels cheap and slightly rough to the touch, not the soft fabric that the pictures suggested. The seams around the cushion area are already showing signs of stress where my weight concentrates, and I’m worried about long-term durability. Assembly was OK if you’re handy, but the parts didn’t feel sturdy and the frame creaked a little the first week I used it.

What bothered me most was the misleading product copy and photos. If the manufacturer had called this a minimalist dining chair with thin padding, I would have understood the lower cost. But advertising it as “plush” and “supportive” set expectations that were never met. For short visits it’s tolerable, but for working from home, long meals, or reading, it’s uncomfortable.

I’m returning it and looking for a chair with actual cushioning and better build quality. Save yourself the hassle and avoid this if comfort is important to you.

The Neato actually picks stuff up. Based on how often I have to empty the seemingly equal-sized dustbins (Neato's may even be larger), I'd estimate the Neato does 10 times the job of the K4. It isn't just because the K4 spends much of its time actually missing spots and taking the same paths over and over. The K4 mostly just picks up dog hair. Actual dirt particles in the bin? Minimal. title: Well written kidnapping story that will keep you guessing.
text:
Amy Gentry's novel, GOOD AS GONE, shares a lot of its plot with other movies and books. It also shares similarities with the true story of the kidnapping of Elizabeth Smart, from her bedroom at night.

A good portion of the story deals with the fallout that is created in the remaining family members when a child goes missing. The part that is similar to other works of fiction deals with how the family copes, when the hoped for miracle happens: the child returns to the family many years later, eliciting both joy and suspicion. The suspicion is driven by thoughts that the returning child (unrecognizable, after so many years) may, in fact, be an imposter.

GOOD AS GONE has excellent, well developed, realistic and sympathetic characters, and a surprise ending that sets it well apart from novels that have come before. The dialogue and family dynamics feel realistic and the author paces it well and keeps you interested and guessing. I enjoyed it.

text:
I purchased this item last month because my daughter has curly hair that tends to get quite tangled and dry after swimming at the local community pool. The product description claimed it was specifically designed to remove chlorine and salt buildup while maintaining the natural moisture barrier of the hair shaft. I was skeptical at first because there are so many shampoo bottles on the market with similar sounding benefits, but I decided to give it a try since the ratings were generally positive and the price point was reasonable compared to high-end salon brands.

The first thing I noticed upon opening the bottle was the scent. It is not overly floral or fruity, which I appreciate. It smells more like a fresh, clean ocean breeze with a hint of mint. It is refreshing and not overpowering, which is important because strong perfumes often linger in hair for days and can be headache-inducing for some people. I let my daughter wash her hair with this product twice a week for the past three weeks, and I have noticed a significant improvement in the manageability of her curls. They feel softer and the definition is much better than when I used our previous brand.

However, I am only giving it four stars instead of five because of the lather. It does not produce as much foam as I expected. For someone who is used to the heavy, dense bubbles from conventional shampoos, this might feel like it is not actually cleaning her hair. I had to apply a larger amount than I normally would to get the feeling of a thorough cleanse. It is not a dealbreaker, but it is something to be aware of. Additionally, while the bottle is durable, the pump mechanism is a bit stiff and requires a bit of pressure to dispense the product. It works, but it is not as smooth as I would like.

Overall, the performance is excellent. The hair feels genuinely clean without being stripped of natural oils, and the frizz has reduced noticeably. I think this is a solid choice for anyone looking for a gentle, effective wash that respects the integrity of curly or textured hair types. It does what it promises, even if the packaging and lather could be slightly better. I would recommend it to friends who struggle with dry, chlorinated hair, but perhaps suggest they start with a small amount to see how their hair reacts to the lower lather formula. It is a good product, just not perfect.

title: A captivatingly beautiful story!
text:
Tethered Angel, by T.M. Brown, is a captivatingly beautiful story, one that captures the reader like a gentle wind and takes them on a journey which must be seen to its end.
Set in the 1950’s and the burgeoning sixties, Tethered Angel follows Angel, the center of this story, an African-American teenage girl who is struggling to find her identity in a culture which is quickly changing, during an era of racism against blacks and the growing equal-rights movement under the leadership of Martin Luther King. Angel finds herself drawn away from her impoverished lifestyle by the taunts and serpentine appeals offered to her by a rich white woman. The woman convinces Angel, more by force than by reason, to travel with her to Europe, to see the world, leaving her mother behind with just a note. The story which ensues embraces the world of a young black girl at a time when racism is still pungent and violent, where people like her are treated as second-rate human beings, and where she learns to discover her strengths. Throughout the story, Angel converses with those she has lost, the dead, but her visitations from the lost and gone are more like guiding spirits, helping her through difficult times. As she grows and as her independent mind sees another road leading away from a world of bigotry and hate, Angel decides she must make it back to her mother, even years later, in spite of her new state of slavery to the rich white woman. The question is how? This is a story about courage, values, belief in oneself, and the persistence often necessary in life to climb one’s mountain. A very good read.

That said, for the price point this jacket delivers solid performance and comfort for casual outdoor activities. text: I’ve read my fair share of self-help books over the years, and most of them either feel like common sense dressed up in fancy jargon or they make you feel worse for not good enough for not being able to “just think positive.” This one is different. “The Power of Now, Is Taking Control of Your Emotions!” landed on my Kindle during a particularly rough patch at work and at home, and I honestly I was skeptical. Another book telling me to calm down? But the moment I started reading, something clicked. It doesn’t just tell you to control your emotions; it actually shows you how to step back from them and observe them without being consumed. The exercises are practical and surprisingly easy to fit into a busy day. I’ve always been someone who reacts first and thinks later, and that pattern has caused me a lot of regret. After working through the first few chapters, I found myself pausing before snapping at my kids or spiraling over a work email. That pause is everything. The author writes with a clear, grounded voice—no spiritual fluff or vague promises. It’s direct and actionable. My anxiety hasn’t vanished overnight, but I now have a real tool to keep it from running the show. I’ve recommended this to three friends already, and two have texted me saying it’s changing how they handle stress. If you’re tired of feeling like your emotions are driving your life, give this a real chance. It’s not a magic fix, but it’s the closest thing I’ve found to a practical manual for emotional freedom. Five stars without hesitation.

Another huge plus: they are truly rust-resistant. I've left them in a humid bathroom for weeks, and they still look brand new. No corrosion, no discoloration. The protective case is a nice bonus for travel, though I mostly keep them in my vanity drawer.

If you have ever been frustrated by tweezers that stop gripping after a month, or that leave you with bruised skin from having to clamp down so hard, stop wasting money. These are built to last. title: excellent read
text:
I rarely write reviews, but this book compelled me to share how much it exceeded my expectations. From the first chapter I was hooked — the pacing is just right, characters feel authentic, and the prose is both elegant and accessible. I found myself staying up later than I intended because I kept telling myself "just one more chapter," and then another.

What I appreciated most was how the author balanced plot momentum with quiet, character-driven moments. The relationships in the story are nuanced; nobody is purely heroic or villainous, and that complexity made the emotional beats land hard. There are lines I highlighted because they captured things I've felt but never quite been able to say. The book also manages to surprise without relying on cheap twists — the revelations arise naturally from the characters' choices, which made them satisfying and believable.

The themes felt timely without being preachy. Issues around identity, belonging, and forgiveness are woven into the narrative in a way that made me reflect on my own life long after I finished. The setting is vividly drawn; I could picture scenes clearly, and certain passages transported me to specific seasons and smells in a way that great novels do.

Formatting and editing were clean—no distracting typos—so my reading flow was uninterrupted. I'm recommending this to friends who like literary fiction with heart and readers who enjoy emotionally intelligent storytelling. If you're looking for a book that will stay with you, provoke thought, and make you care about its characters, this is an excellent read. I plan to keep a copy on my shelf and revisit it in the future.

title: Colored natural, kinky hair
text:
I have bleached and colored natural, kinky hair. This is the first time I've ever colored my hair and I made sure to do my research on colored hair care, which includes protein treatments. Well, months had gone by and I still hadn't done a protein treatment. Madness, right? Eventually, the dyed parts (especially the ends) started to feel rough and dry.The ends were also knotting like crazy! I remembered a YouTube video I watched about hydrolyzed wheat protein. I ordered that and a pair of hair shears (prepared to do some clipping, which I had also been neglecting). I heard that you should expect to see results after the first use, but I was blown away! First, I cleansed my hair with shampoo. I didn't measure how much of the treatment I used but I mixed it in with my regular, wash out conditioner. After coating my hair in it, I covered my hair with a plastic cap then sat with my conditioning heat cap on my head for about 15 minutes.
My hair in general, not only the dyed area, feels softer and the colored ends feel smooth and manageable again. Also, waaaaay less knotting. After washing my hair, I put it in twists to dry. 2 days later I pulled out the twists to get a lovely, voluminous twist-out. Unfortunately, I didn't get the shears but Amazon promptly refunded me and I plan to reorder them shortly. I'm ashamed to say its been months since my ends have been clipped (which just compounded the problem) and I plan to use my protein treatment around once a month and trim when needed.

text:
I was hesitant to buy a third-party band for my Garmin Vivofit, but I've had for over two years, but this replacement exceeded every expectation. This band fits my Vivofit 3 perfectly, and installation was as simple as popping the tracker out and popping the tracker out of the old band and snapping it into this one. No tools or adapters required.

The material feels noticeably more durable than the factory band. It has a nice matte finish that doesn't show fingerprints or scratches, and the metal buckle is a huge upgrade over the plastic one that broke on my original. I've been wearing it daily for three weeks, including during sweaty workouts and while sleeping, and there's no skin irritation or discoloration. The sizing holes are well-spaced, allowing a comfortable fit for my wrist without being too loose or too tight.

For the price, this band is an incredible value. My only minor observation is that the color is slightly darker than the product images, but it still looks clean and professional. If you need a reliable replacement for your Vivofit replacement band, don't hesitate to try this one. It's already outlasted the original, and I plan to buy another as a backup.

title: The Eternal Truth of the Simple Man
text:
Norwood Pratt has neither guile nor an education, but he possesses a comic wisdom that guides him from one nutty encounter to another. He is the man he is, regardless, slow to fight but ready to fight, honest, to a point, and rationalizing beyond that. He never internalizes, seldom jumps to conclusions, and just proceeds along the rightness of his course without question. He is a Faulknerian character distilled down to the basics, so unsophisticated he is hilariously honest.

Norwood is a fast-paced comedy of the simpleton winning out in the end because his sights are so low he can't lose, and Charles Portis' social commentary should not be missed, but if you do, the dialogue alone is worth the read. And if the characters in Norwood seem too silly to be real? Well, I recognized them more than I care to admit.

title: Great Hold and Light Scent
text:
I have been using beard oil for a while, but recently, it was not making the cut and my beard was getting a little too scraggly for work. I decided to try beard balm to see if it might be able to provide some hold and tame down some of my loose hairs. I was worried that I would need a significant trim if I couldn't find a way to bring it all together, but since starting to use this balm daily, I have been able to let it grow without any thoughts about the professionalism. Below are a few comments I have to make on different aspects of this balm.

Size: This is a fairly large container. If you are looking for some size comparisons, I would say it is about the same diameter as a coffee cup and 3/4 of an inch deep. I have been using it daily for a few weeks now and still have well over 90% of the balm remaining.

Scent: As someone switching from beard oils with fairly strong scents, I initially thought this balm was scentless. I think this can be a positive or a negative depending on your preferences. If you are using a beard oil or cologne with a scent you love, this will not clash with it, but will give you the hold and conditioning you are looking for. On the other hand, if you are looking for a balm that will double as cologne, you'll probably want to buy a beard oil or some actual cologne to supplement what this will provide.

Strength: The hold is great! My beard is about an inch and a half to two inches, and this has provided the perfect amount of hold for me. It helps me to be able to do a little bit of shaping when I need to, but mostly allows my beard to be itself. It has also left my beard feeling less dry and looking a little bit healthier.

Overall, this is a great beard balm and I would recommend it to first time users or those who have tried many before. Also, I received this balm in exchange for an honest review.

text:

This harness keeps her in check without choking or hurting her and I like it alot. It is easy to adjust and not visibly uncomfortable to her, never chokes her. She can eat or drink with it on. Walks are much easier. By controlling her head, her pulling is inhibited and she is more prone to listen to training commands. Squirrels or other dogs still get her excited and she will pull initially but if I use a shorter grip on the leash, she obeys. When we walk and she starts to tug, I stop walking and she relents. Pulling is never zero, but it is much more brief.

Others wrote that dogs can get the harness off and yes, if I don't pay attention she has tried to push it off her nose with her paw. A little correction stops that and we continue our walks.

It doesn't appear uncomfortable but she would prefer not to have any leash on of course. I only use the trainer on a leash, she doesn't wear it all the time and when I bring out the leash for walk time, she sits and waits to get it on. I tried a pinch collar in the past, she was definitely unwillingly to have that put on and would run to her kennel instead. Contrarily, she is eager to get this harness on and go for a walk anytime.

Walks are pleasurable again and we use it daily. Highly recommend.

title: If I Stay
text:
In If I Stay, we meet Mia, a very talented cellist, who is in love with a boy who wants to be a rock star. They find their lives being pulled in two different directions. Mia hopes to go to Juilliard and Adam, her boyfriend, hopes to take his band to the highest points in the industry. Until everything changes for both of them. Mia's family is in a car accident and then she is left in a coma. While her body lies limp in a hospital bed, she finds herself taking a journey to figure out if she should leave everything on earth behind to be with her family, who are already gone, or stay and be with those who are there praying and hoping she will return. This story isn't just about love and loss, its about impossible choices and heartbreak. No matter what Mia's choice, she feels that she loses a piece of herself.

We follow Mia througout the book on a journey through her memories, making you better understand how badly she will break if she wakes up and has lost her family. We also see her relationship with Adam and how much they truly care about each other and how their lives are clearly drifting in different directions.This story is painful just to read but beautifully written and really hits its mark in making you sit at the edge of your seat to see which avenue she will choose.

title: You get what you pay for
text: I bought this game for a low price, and honestly, you get what you pay for. The pieces are flimsy plastic, and the box arrived slightly crushed. The instructions are poorly translated and hard to follow. My kids lost interest after one round because the spinner broke. For the cost-effective for a quick distraction, but I wouldn’t gift it. Fine for the price, but temper your expectations.

text: I bought this for our kitchen a few weeks ago and it's been a delightful surprise. The quality is evident from the moment you unpack it — sturdy, well-made, and exactly as described. title: Leans forward, hard seat
text: I bought this chair hoping for a simple, comfortable upgrade for my home office, but it’s been a big disappointment. The seat pitches forward so much my hips slide and I feel like I’m constantly sliding toward the desk. The padding is thin and hard — not at all cushioned — so after 20–30 minutes my lower back and tailbone ache. Assembly was okay, but comfort is the whole point and this fails. Returning it. Would not recommend unless you like sitting on a firm, angled plank.

text: I’ve tried several products for my anxious dog and this one really works. Within a few days his trembling and pacing decreased noticeably, and he’s sleeping through storms now. The spray is easy to apply and doesn’t irritate his skin or leave a strong smell. Packaging was secure and arrived quickly. I’m relieved to have found something reliable — definitely worth the purchase for pets with anxiety.

text: I use this at work. I had the original Wireless Elite and I have to say this on improves on it in almost every way. The USB dongle is a lot smaller and they ditched the super bright and annoying blue LED. Keys are soft and the over all design is slim and light-weight. Its actually lighter than the original Elite Keyboard.It even has a battery life indicator that the oolder one did not have. Its a joy to use and type on all day long at work.

title: Used in a Nitro Venom air rifle trigger
text: I installed these springs in my Nitro Venom to smooth out the heavy factory trigger. The pull weight dropped noticeably, making it much easier to squeeze without disturbing the sight picture. The texture is a bit rougher than premium aftermarket options, but they seat well in the original housing. It’s a solid budget upgrade for an older airgun that I don’t want to invest hundreds in modifying. If you want a cleaner break for less money, this does the job adequately. Not perfect, but definitely an improvement over stock.

title: Doesn't disolve & hard to rinse out of the tub
text: I bought this hoping for a relaxing bath, but it was a total nightmare. The product claims to dissolve easily, but that is absolutely not the case. I dropped it in the water and instead of holding it under the faucet, and even after ten minutes, chunks were still floating around. I had to stir aggressively and even crush bits got stuck to my skin. Worse, when I drained the tub, a thick, slimy residue was left coating the entire surface. It took me nearly twenty minutes with a scrub brush and multiple rinses to get it off. The residue also left a weird film on my hair and skin that wouldn't rinse clean. I feel like I wasted my bathtub is now stained and I’m worried about clogged pipes. For a product in the "All Beauty" category, this is far from a beauty experience—it's a chore. Save your money and your sanity. Absolutely will not repurchase.

title: Meade Infinity 102mm AZ Refractor
text: I didn't have good luck with this telescope.  When you find something in the sky and try and lock it in with the stand it came with ,  it would move and you would loose what you are looking at.  I didn't think it was that powerful.  I saw almost as much with my binoculars.  So I sent mine back.  I will save up and buy a bigger one.  It seemed well made except the stand.  I am not that much of an expert so if others give it a better review go by their review more than mine. Meade has a good reputation for quality so look at their other telescopes also.  I went to an astronomy forums site. They recommended for me a dobsonian  style.  The base is usually more stable if you go with a 6-12"  depending on your budget you will see a lot more than with this one.  They are also bigger and take more to set up so take that into consideration.

title: NOT good for security, good for deliveries. Two massive flaws.
text:
This could be a five star product.

I was SHOCKED to discover that the Blink monitor has two fatal flaws: 1) There is no alarm. Who could possibly design a product like this, and not have an alarm feature. You can't arm it when you sleep so your phone will ring like crazy if motion is detected. 2) The notification sound CANNOT be customized. This is beyond stupid. The notification sound is the same generic sound you'll get for all other notifications, so you won't be able to tell if it's your Blink monitor, or today's news that your phone is alerting you of.

I would imagine both of these problems can be fixed with software updates. And I thought about buying a Ring, but I don't they have alarm features either. Absolutely insane. But despite all this, for what it does, it works well and it's considerably cheaper than a ring.
